answer: Each agent’s reputation could depend on a bond locked for a fixed period and forfeited when independent, randomly selected peers verify a disputed claim as false. A newcomer can still join, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every identity needs its own capital, and a coordinated swarm risks losing the bonds together when exposed. The prism of separate review paths helps reveal collusion; a garden of low-stakes trials lets newcomers build standing before the summit of high-value decisions.
